overview: XD Inc. is a Shanghai-based Chinese mobile/PC game developer and publisher that also operates TapTap, a game discovery, distribution and community platform with separate PRC and international versions. The company's two segments are symbiotic: self-developed and licensed games (life-sim Heartopia, Torchlight: Infinite, Ragnarok M franchise) generate exclusive content that drives traffic to TapTap, while TapTap's advertising and distribution business monetizes that audience and funds further game development. XD is HKEX-listed (Cayman-incorporated, PRC operating entities via consolidated affiliated entities), reports in RMB with a December fiscal year-end, and generates the large majority of revenue domestically with a growing but still small international games/platform footprint.

business_model.summary: Two reinforcing segments: Games (online in-game virtual item sales plus premium pay-to-play titles, ~66% of FY2025 revenue) and TapTap platform (primarily online marketing/advertising services monetizing a free, zero-revenue-share game discovery app, ~34% of FY2025 revenue and growing faster and at much higher margin). TapTap's refusal to take a developer revenue share is a deliberate growth/ecosystem strategy, monetizing instead through ads and now a nascent PC storefront and AI tools (TapTap Maker).
business_model.customer_type: B2C (game players, both free-to-play with IAP and premium pay-to-play) and B2B (game developers/advertisers on TapTap)
business_model.geographic_mix: Predominantly Chinese Mainland for both games and TapTap PRC; growing but unmonetized international footprint via TapTap International (3-5m MAU) and overseas game launches (Southeast Asia, HK/Macau/Taiwan, Japan/Korea, and a January 2026 global Heartopia launch); revenue recognized on a 'net basis' (indicating overseas third-party distribution, e.g. Apple/Google app stores) rose sharply in 2025 on Ragnarok M: Classic's overseas performance.

main_competitors: Huawei AppGallery / Chinese Android app stores
competitive_position.market_position: XD is a mid-sized, independent Chinese game developer/publisher (far smaller than Tencent or NetEase) whose principal differentiator is TapTap, the leading independent (non-phone-maker, non-Tencent) game discovery and community platform in China, built on a decade-long zero-revenue-share model that has made it a trusted channel for indie and mid-tier developers. XD's own game portfolio (22-23 online titles, 45-52 premium titles) is diversified beyond a single hit after a multi-year post-COVID adjustment.

moat_factors.description: TapTap has never taken a cut of developer IAP revenue, in contrast to phone-maker app stores and Tencent's distribution channels; this has built a decade of developer trust and switching costs that are hard for a new entrant to replicate without foregoing the same revenue

TapTap functions as a reviews/ratings/community hub (akin to a gaming-specific app store plus forum), creating a flywheel where quality content attracts players, players attract more developers, and engagement data improves ad targeting

moat_factors.factor: Vertical integration of publishing and platform
moat_factors.description: XD's own hit games (Heartopia, Torchlight: Infinite, Ragnarok M family) give TapTap exclusive, high-quality content that pure third-party platforms lack, while TapTap in turn cross-promotes XD's titles

The December 2025 acquisition of the full Torchlight IP (for ~US$37.2m, offset against a loan to the seller) removes royalty payments and gives XD a permanent, wholly-owned franchise it can invest behind long-term

TapTap recognized as China's leading independent game discovery app after ten years (2026 marks its 10th anniversary), but its PRC MAU growth has plateaued (~45m, high single-digit growth) as domestic penetration matures

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on a small number of top-5 games for the large majority of game revenue; any decline in Heartopia, Torchlight: Infinite or the Ragnarok M franchise disproportionately affects results

TapTap International remains unmonetized after years of operation and its MAU has been declining (down 37.9% YoY in H1 2026), showing limited traction against established global discovery/community channels (Discord, Steam, YouTube/Twitch, Reddit)

No revenue-share model means TapTap's own monetization is capped at advertising yield, a structurally lower-margin, more cyclical revenue pool than a typical app-store commission model used by larger peers
Small scale versus Tencent/NetEase limits bargaining power with top global IP holders and ability to out-bid for blockbuster licenses
Online game MAUs/MPUs fell ~20% in FY2025 as Heartopia and Sausage Man usage normalized post-launch, underscoring the volatility of mobile hit-driven revenue

growth_drivers: Heartopia's January 2026 global expansion beyond Chinese Mainland, leveraging over a year of player feedback from the domestic launch
Torchlight IP now wholly owned, enabling larger long-term investment in seasonal content without royalty drag and supporting the franchise's push to become an 'evergreen' title
Ragnarok M: Eternal Love 2 relaunch across Southeast Asia, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, intended to become XD's own enduring RO sub-IP with an independent ecosystem

TapTap PC rollout (launched April 2025) carrying the zero-revenue-share model into PC gaming, creating a new distribution leg and cross-platform progress-sync features (e.g., Dave the Diver mobile/PC sync)

TapTap Maker, an AI game-creation agent launched for invitation testing in January 2026, aiming to materially lower the cost/skill barrier to creating games and expand the pipeline of exclusive content feeding TapTap (over 6,000 games built on the agent as of the H1 2026 report)

Continued AI integration across R&D, operations and advertising algorithms (XD also open-sourced an internal AI office-work agent, 'Cindy', in July 2026) aimed at efficiency gains and new monetizable products
Premium (pay-to-play) game publishing expansion on both PC and mobile, growing TapTap's content diversity and cross-platform ecosystem
Capital-light growth strategy: no borrowings, ~RMB3.9bn net cash, funding games/IP/AI investment from operating cash flow

business.description: Top five games drive the large majority of game revenue; Heartopia and Sausage Man usage declines in FY2025 illustrate how quickly a hit can fade without continuous content refreshes
These larger rivals have vastly greater capital, IP portfolios and user reach, and compete for both players and top developer content that could otherwise anchor TapTap
International MAU has declined for multiple consecutive periods and remains unmonetized; limited resource allocation suggests management is not prioritizing a turnaround near-term

business.risk: AI-era disruption to game creation and discovery
business.description: A flood of AI-generated games (including via XD's own TapTap Maker) could commoditize content and increase competition for player attention and ad inventory even as it also benefits TapTap's ecosystem strategy

financial.description: Overseas revenue and USD-denominated licensing fees/IP payments create unhedged currency exposure (primarily USD and HKD); the company does not use hedging instruments

A large swing between gross- and net-basis revenue recognition (net-basis share rose from 4.3% to 13.5% of game operating revenue in FY2025 on overseas RO: Classic performance, then fell back in H1 2026) adds variability to reported margins period to period

regulatory.description: Games released or monetized in Mainland China generally require an NPPA publishing license; approval timing and content restrictions (e.g., anti-addiction, minors' protection rules) can delay or block launches and are outside the company's control
Chinese regulators have historically imposed playtime and spending limits on minors, which can structurally cap monetization of certain titles

TapTap's advertising business is subject to PRC rules on online advertising, data privacy and algorithmic recommendation systems, any tightening of which could raise compliance costs or limit targeting effectiveness

As with most China internet-sector HKEX/ADR listings, XD operates certain PRC businesses through consolidated affiliated entities (VIE-like arrangements) that carry inherent legal and enforceability uncertainty

macro.description: In-game purchases and premium game sales are discretionary spending exposed to a slower Chinese consumer/macro backdrop
TapTap's ad revenue depends on developer marketing budgets, which can contract in a weaker game-launch or funding environment

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's game approval pace has accelerated in 2026 (NPPA approvals up ~19% YoY, on track for over 2,300 games approved in the year), suggesting a generally supportive regulatory backdrop for new content versus the more restrictive 2021-2022 period; global discovery/publishing is increasingly AI-assisted, which is a structural tailwind for TapTap's content-supply strategy if it can capture the resulting wave of new titles
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate; mobile game revenue is hit-driven and can be lumpy around launch cycles and content updates, while advertising revenue on TapTap has some cyclicality tied to developer marketing budgets
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity; the company carries no borrowings and holds a large net cash position, so earnings are not levered to interest costs
key_input_costs: Cloud service, bandwidth and server custody fees
Game development/outsourcing and art production costs
Revenue-sharing/distribution-platform commissions paid to app stores and payment channels
AI compute/token costs (rising, per management commentary on R&D expense growth)

recent_developments.event: Interim report for H1 2026 filed; revenue up 7.5% YoY to RMB3.31bn but profit down 10.6% YoY to RMB724.3m, as rising AI-related R&D spend and higher distribution commissions compressed margins despite game revenue growth

Goldman Sachs upgraded XD to Buy (trimming price target to HK$60.7 on a SOTP basis), citing an expected growth inflection from H2 2026 despite near-term earnings pressure from AI spending and traffic competition between AI-made and commercial games
XD open-sourced 'Cindy,' an internal AI office-work agent, as part of its broader push to productize internal AI tooling
TapTap PC entered its second year of rollout with growing developer cooperation and user base; mobile version of Dave the Diver launched with cross-device progress sync to TapTap PC

Heartopia launched globally (outside Chinese Mainland) after refinement based on over a year of domestic player feedback; TapTap Maker (AI game-creation agent) began invitation-only testing, with over 6,000 games built on it by mid-2026

XD acquired full ownership of the Torchlight game IP and related intangible assets for ~US$37.2m, settled by offsetting a loan previously extended to the seller (Golden Arc/Runic Games/Arc Games), eliminating future royalty payments
Relaunch of Ragnarok M: Classic across Southeast Asia, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan performed well, prompting XD to brand its RO line as an independent sub-IP ('Ragnarok M: Eternal Love 2')

Full-year results: revenue RMB5.76bn (+15% YoY), net profit RMB1.66bn (+86% YoY), gross margin improved to 73.8% from 69.4%, driven by TapTap's 24.7% platform revenue growth and a richer overseas net-basis revenue mix

Company shifted capital returns from cash dividends toward an ongoing share repurchase-and-cancellation programme (HK$400m+ authorized; ~HK$493m repurchased and cancelled in H1 2026 alone), citing tax efficiency for shareholders

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report (filed ~August/October 2026) and FY2025 Annual Report Chairman's Letter

items.target: Ongoing share repurchases and cancellations in lieu of traditional cash dividends
items.notes: Management explicitly stated intent to replace dividends with buybacks as a more tax-efficient shareholder return; board resolved not to declare an interim dividend for H1 2026

items.target: Continue introducing more high-quality PC and mobile premium titles
items.notes: No specific revenue number; qualitative commitment to expand premium game line following FY2025's 15.6% premium game revenue growth

items.target: Expand invitation testing of TapTap Maker and deepen AI integration across dev/publishing/ops workflows
items.notes: No monetization targets disclosed yet; framed as a long-term ecosystem/content-supply strategy rather than a near-term revenue driver

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Huang Yimeng's FY2025 letter emphasized a more resilient, less single-hit-dependent game portfolio, the strategic value of owning the Torchlight IP outright, and a pivot toward AI (TapTap Maker, internal AI tooling) as the next decade's growth vector for TapTap beyond pure discovery. Management acknowledged TapTap PRC's domestic penetration is reaching a ceiling and that further growth requires 'a more significant breakthrough' via enabling game creation itself, not just discovery. External analysts (Goldman Sachs) flagged near-term margin pressure from AI compute spend and increased competition for player traffic between AI-made and traditional commercial games, but expect a growth inflection from H2 2026 onward.

bull_case: TapTap's zero-revenue-share model and decade of accumulated developer trust give it a durable, hard-to-replicate position in Chinese game discovery, with platform revenue still growing faster (+24.7% FY2025) than the games business and at much higher incremental margin

Portfolio diversification away from single-hit dependency (Heartopia, Torchlight: Infinite, Ragnarok M family all contributing) plus full ownership of the Torchlight IP removes royalty drag and supports higher long-term reinvestment conviction
Clean balance sheet with no debt and ~RMB3.9bn net cash gives flexibility to fund R&D, bolt-on IP acquisitions (like Torchlight) and shareholder returns simultaneously

Early-mover position in AI-assisted game creation (TapTap Maker) could materially expand the volume and diversity of exclusive content feeding the platform, reinforcing the publishing-platform flywheel ahead of competitors

Shift to buybacks-and-cancellation as the primary capital return vehicle is shareholder-friendly and tax-efficient, and FY2025's 86% net profit growth and margin expansion (gross margin 69.4% to 73.8%) show the operating leverage in the model when hits land
bear_case: H1 2026 showed revenue growth decoupling from profit (revenue +7.5%, profit -10.6%) as AI-related R&D and distribution costs rose faster than revenue, raising the question of whether AI investment will structurally compress margins before it pays off

TapTap International has failed to gain traction for years (MAU down 37.9% YoY in H1 2026) and remains entirely unmonetized, suggesting the platform's moat may not travel outside China against entrenched global alternatives

Online game user metrics fell sharply in FY2025 (MAUs -20.4%, MPUs -20.2%) as Heartopia's initial launch surge faded, underscoring the fragility of mobile hit-driven revenue and the need for constant new content to sustain engagement

XD remains a minnow relative to Tencent, NetEase and miHoYo in capital, global IP access and user reach, limiting its ability to win bidding wars for blockbuster licenses or match their marketing scale

PRC content-approval licensing, minors' protection rules and advertising/data regulation remain an ever-present overhang on both the games and TapTap advertising businesses, even though the 2026 approval pace has been comparatively benign
